title: Roasted Tomato & White Bean Skillet
description: Jammy tomatoes, creamy white beans, and crisp garlic crumbs in a weeknight skillet that wants a piece of toast.
notes: Use gluten-free crumbs or skip the topping if needed. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within four days.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Warm 1 tablespoon olive oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a few begin to split. Add two-thirds of the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in the beans, broth, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 3 minutes, gently crushing a few beans to thicken the liquid.
Mix the panko with the remaining olive oil and garlic. Scatter it over the skillet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the tomatoes are jammy. Rest for 5 minutes and finish with parsley.

title: Charred Corn & Avocado Tacos
description: Sweet charred corn, creamy avocado, crunchy cabbage, and a bright lime crema tucked into warm tortillas.
notes: For a dairy-free version, use an unsweetened plant-based yogurt labeled safe for your needs.
instructions: Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add the oil and corn, spread it into one layer, and cook without stirring for 3 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder and salt, then cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until the corn is deeply browned in spots.
Stir the yogurt with the zest and juice of one lime and a pinch of salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame, turning carefully with tongs.
Fill each tortilla with cabbage, charred corn, avocado, lime crema, and cilantro. Serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

title: Lemon-Herb Sheet-Pan Chicken & Potatoes
description: Crisp-edged potatoes and juicy lemon-herb chicken roast together while a quick pan sauce builds underneath.
notes: Cook chicken to 165°F in the thickest part. Wash hands and surfaces after handling raw poultry.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half the salt, and half the pepper on a rimmed sheet pan.
Roast the potatoes cut-side down for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, zest and juice the lemon. Mix the zest, half the juice, garlic, thyme, remaining oil, salt, and pepper. Coat the chicken with the mixture.
Turn the potatoes, add the chicken and broccoli, and roast for 20 to 25 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are tender.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes. Spoon the remaining lemon juice and pan juices over everything before serving.

title: Ginger-Sesame Noodles with Crisp Vegetables
description: A fast tangle of noodles, crunchy vegetables, and a savory ginger-sesame dressing that works warm or chilled.
notes: Check noodle and soy sauce labels carefully for wheat if adapting this recipe for gluten-free needs.
instructions: Cook the noodles in salted water according to the package directions. Reserve 1/2 cup cooking water, then drain.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, and ginger in a large bowl.
Add the warm noodles and toss, loosening with a splash of cooking water if needed.
Fold in the carrot, bell pepper, cucumber, and scallions. Taste and adjust with more vinegar or soy sauce.
Finish with sesame seeds. Serve warm, at room temperature, or chilled.

title: Creamy Red Lentil Tomato Soup
description: Red lentils melt into tomato and warm spices for a silky pantry soup with no cream required.
notes: Cool leftovers in shallow containers and refrigerate within two hours. Blend carefully to avoid hot splashes.
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots with a pinch of salt for 7 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, broth, and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cover partially and cook for 20 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the lentils are completely tender.
Blend until mostly smooth, keeping some texture. Stir in the lemon juice and adjust the seasoning.

title: Apple-Cinnamon Baked Oats
description: Soft-centered baked oats with apples, warm spice, and a crisp walnut top for an easy make-ahead breakfast.
notes: Omit walnuts for a nut-free version and check every packaged ingredient for cross-contact information.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter an 8-inch baking dish.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt in the dish.
Whisk the milk, egg, maple syrup, butter, and vanilla in a bowl.
Scatter the apples over the oats, pour in the milk mixture, and gently stir. Top with walnuts if using.
Bake for 32 to 36 minutes, until the center is set and the edges are golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Crispy Chickpea & Cucumber Bowls
description: Spiced crispy chickpeas, cool cucumber, greens, and lemony tahini over rice for a satisfying bowl with plenty of crunch.
notes: Tahini contains sesame. Use a different dressing if sesame is unsafe for you.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, cumin, paprika, and salt on a sheet pan.
Roast for 22 to 26 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until crisp at the edges.
Whisk the tahini with the lemon zest, lemon juice, and water. Add more water a teaspoon at a time until pourable.
Divide the rice, cucumber, and greens among bowls.
Top with the warm chickpeas and drizzle with lemon-tahini sauce.

title: Brown Butter Miso Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy chocolate chip cookies with nutty brown butter and a small spoonful of miso for a deeper caramel edge.
notes: Miso contains soy. Let the brown butter cool before adding the egg so it does not scramble.
instructions: Melt the butter in a light-colored saucepan over medium heat. Cook, swirling often, until the milk solids turn amber and smell nutty. Pour into a mixing bowl and cool for 15 minutes.
Whisk the miso, brown sugar, and granulated sugar into the butter. Whisk in the egg and vanilla until glossy.
Fold in the flour, baking soda, and salt, then fold in the chocolate chips. Chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line two sheet pans with parchment. Scoop the dough into 2-tablespoon portions spaced 2 inches apart.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers still look soft. Cool on the pan for 5 minutes before moving to a rack.
